Food items which I had are as follows:

•Chicken Chetinad: 5/5
Chicken Chetinad is a gravy made with boneless chicken pieces, turmeric, and coconut paste. This gravy was full of flavors and it was super delicious with paratha. In quantity wise I feel maximum 3 people can have it. Paratha was flaky, crispy and cooked well.

•Chicken Ghee Roast: 3/5
Soft juicy boneless chicken pieces roasted in ghee and in a sweet gravy.I had this with appam which is very much similar to a plain dosa but it also has coconut milk to it which makes it a bit on sweeter side.
Personally this dish was very sweet and sweetness should be reduced.

•Mangalorean Chicken: 4/5
Mangalorean chicken was so flavorful and tasty. It had all the delicious combinations right from the down South. Aroma & taste of coconut milk with spices to the gravy was such a delight to taste buds. I had this paratha and appam.

•Steamed Rice: 5/5
A small bowl full of plain cooked rice. Quality of the rice was good and it went really well with all the above dishes.

•Papd: 5/5
It was thin crispy and fried well.

I’d recommend people ordering food from here to have Chicken Chetinad, Mangalorean Chicken, Steamed Rice and Papad.

featured_reviews.name: Prabhjit Singh Modi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dosa and Thatte Idli both of them were good. What they could really add to the menu is some basic empathy.

I came from Vadodara after a 6-hour train journey and reached around 5:45 am. This was the first place I walked into straight from the railway station. At 6:00 am I politely asked the manager, the one with specs, if I could just sit in the corner since the space was empty and their setup was done. He flatly refused and said I could only enter at 7:00 am.

My back was hurting after the journey and I just needed a place to sit for a bit. It wouldn’t have cost them anything to show a little understanding. Instead, it was a straight no, no conversation.

If this were a smaller outlet, I’m pretty sure someone would’ve just said, “Haan bhai, sit.” Instead, he just didn’t allow it. No explanation, no actual rule, just a straight no. The place was empty, I wasn’t asking for free food, just a corner for 60 minutes after a 6-hour train ride. It honestly felt unnecessary and ego-driven.

That’s what happens when brands get big. A little success and suddenly basic decency becomes optional and Money gets to their head.

Massive respect though to the slim guy who seemed like the asst manager. He kept asking if I wanted to sit on his bike outside. That genuinely melted my heart. At least someone there understood basic humanity.

Food is good. The attitude needs serious work.

Uppu — A strong South Indian addition at Reclamation
Stopped by Uppu for a quick pit stop and came away genuinely impressed. The location is extremely convenient, especially if you’re around Reclamation and looking for quality South Indian food without overthinking it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
UPPU – A South Indian Kitchen in Bandra West is truly one of those rare places that gets everything right. I happened to visit UPPU in the last week of January 2026. From the moment you step in, the ambience immediately sets the tone. It’s warm, inviting, and thoughtfully designed — giving you a sense of comfort that makes you want to sit back and enjoy your meal without any rush. The interiors have a subtle South Indian touch, yet feel modern and elegant at the same time.

The food is where UPPU really shines. The taste is genuinely authentic — you can tell that attention has been paid to traditional recipes and flavours. Every dish feels carefully prepared, balanced, and true to its roots. The spices are not overpowering, the flavours are layered, and the overall experience feels wholesome rather than heavy. It’s the kind of place where you don’t just eat, you savour.

Another thing that stood out for me was the service. The staff is extremely well mannered, polite, and attentive. What I particularly appreciated is that they are present when needed but never intrusive. They don’t interrupt your dining or conversations unnecessarily, which makes the overall experience even more pleasant. It’s rare to find that perfect balance of attentiveness without interference.

Despite being located in Bandra West, where restaurants are plenty and competition is high, UPPU manages to create its own identity. It feels premium yet comfortable, refined yet relaxed. Whether you’re visiting for a family dinner, a quiet catch-up with friends, or even a business conversation, the setting works beautifully.

UPPU is a wonderful South Indian Restaurant and is definitely a place I would visit again and highly recommend to anyone looking for quality dining in Bandra West.

If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently, I had the pleasure of dining at Hoppumm, a cozy Sri Lankan restaurant tucked away in Khar West.

The moment we stepped in, we were greeted with a warm and lively ambiance – minimalist yet vibrant decor that instantly transported us to the streets of Shrilanka.

Ambiance and Setting:
The interiors are stylish yet casual, perfect for a relaxed evening. Beautifully painted walls, masks hanged on the wall and subtle lighting created an inviting atmosphere.

Service:
The service was quick, efficient, and polite. Special thanks to Mr. Imran for his wonderful hospitality — he patiently introduced us to the different dishes and ensured prompt service throughout the evening, making our experience even more memorable.

Food Quality:
We tried a variety of dishes:

Pineapple & Basil Cooler (refreshing and balanced)

Kokum Sharbat (perfectly tangy and cooling)

Chicken & Cheese Kottu (a hearty, flavorful dish and is a MUST TRY)

Lankan Stewed Chilli Chicken (rich coconut broth with tender chicken)

Green Mango Chicken Curry (tangy, creamy curry served in a portion fit for one person)

Traditional Hopper (light and crispy, served along with Podi)

Hot Butter Squid (crispy yet juicy with a burst of flavors)

Lemony Chicken Delight Combo (the showstopper with a perfect balance of zest and spice. There were many different dishes added to rice including a fried chicken leg piece)

They also offered three different types of chatneys from spicy to sweet flavour and you can add according to your need.
Food wasn't much spicy.

Each dish was authentic, beautifully presented, and packed with bold flavors true to Sri Lankan cuisine. Portion sizes were quite satisfying for the price.

Hoppumm is a hidden gem for those looking to explore Sri Lankan cuisine in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Hoppum, a true haven for authentic Sri Lankan cuisine, and it was quite the culinary journey!

We began with the Lankan Stewed Chilli Chicken, where tender chicken was stuffed into green chillies — a brilliant fusion of juicy meat, aromatic spices, and bold chilli heat. It set the tone for what we hoped would be an exciting meal.

The Chicken and Cheese Kottu followed, a popular Sri Lankan street dish featuring finely chopped roti tossed with vegetables and chicken. It was delicious, evoking nostalgic Indian chaat vibes (think ragda pattice) with its hearty and comforting flavors.

The Green Mango Chicken Curry was a standout — silky smooth, subtly tangy with green mango, and enriched with coconut. Paired with their traditional Hopper (similar to an appam), it was an absolute treat.

We also tried the Hot Butter Squid, which was flavorful and perfectly chewy — a must for seafood enthusiasts.

Portion sizes for starters felt on the smaller side, especially considering the price point. Another important thing to note was the food was pre-prepared, and simply heated and served.

To beat the heat, the bottled Pineapple & Basil Cooler and Kokum Sherbet provided much-needed refreshment.

Our meal wrapped up with the Lemony Chicken Delight Combo Rice, served beautifully in a banana leaf with rice, chicken leg, coconut chutneys, and garnishes. Unfortunately, while visually appealing, it lacked the bold flavors we anticipated and felt a bit bland.

While the restaurant greets you with a pleasant, warm ambiance, the seating feels quite congested. The small tables and pocket-café vibe were a bit of a letdown, especially for a place that serves such vibrant cuisine.

The decor and overall aesthetic of this place are truly beautiful. The ambiance, design, and attention to detail make it feel like a high-end spot, and walking in, you definitely expect a premium dining experience. Unfortunately, while the space looks stunning, the actual experience did not live up to the expectations, especially considering the reputation and standard one would associate with a place like this.

The biggest issue by far was the number of bugs. There were so many insects flying around our table while we were eating, which completely ruined the experience. What made it even more uncomfortable was that the staff were actively killing bugs right next to us as we were dining, which felt extremely unhygienic and honestly quite disgusting. It completely took away from the enjoyment of the meal and made it hard to relax or even finish our food comfortably. For a restaurant of this level, this is simply unacceptable and needs serious attention.

In terms of the food, it was a mixed experience. The watermelon and pineapple juices were good — fresh, refreshing, and nicely prepared. The watermelon salad, however, lacked flavor and felt quite underwhelming, especially given how promising it sounded on the menu.

We ordered the edamame peas and the spicy chicken, and those dishes were actually quite good. They were well-cooked, flavorful, and enjoyable, which showed that the kitchen does have potential. However, good dishes alone cannot make up for poor hygiene standards and an uncomfortable dining environment.

The service also felt below expectation. It didn’t reflect the quality, attentiveness, or polish you would normally associate with a Bastian-level standard. Overall, the experience felt disorganized and lacking in the fine-dining attention to detail that one would expect.

In summary, while the decor is stunning and some of the food items were good, the bug issue and service quality seriously impacted the experience. It did not feel like a Bastian-standard restaurant, and until these issues are resolved, it’s hard to recommend. With better hygiene control, improved service, and more consistency in food quality, this place could truly live up to its potential — but for now, it unfortunately falls short.

We recently visited Freny’s All Day Dining Bar on Linking Road, Bandra West, and absolutely loved the experience! The space is warm, inviting, and thoughtfully designed — it truly feels like walking into someone’s charming East Indian home.
The interiors are a beautiful blend of retro, European, Portuguese, and East Indian décor — from pastel colors and vintage chandeliers to framed family photos and wallpapered ceilings. The ground floor gives off cosy café vibes, while the upper floor offers a more formal dining space with a well-stocked bar and nostalgic touches throughout. Every corner tells a story!
We tried a variety of items and everything was delicious:
Mocktails: Chocolate Skyline, Boozy Bougie Pop, Rose Ciel – all refreshing and unique!
Desserts: Tiramisu Dreamin, Caramel Apple, Cheese Basque Cake, Jardin Du Rose, and the star of the show — Matilda’s Chocolate Cake. Rich, moist, and absolutely unforgettable — hands down one of the best cakes we’ve had!
They also serve traditional East Indian dishes like fugiyas, alongside modern café-style fare including pizzas, burgers, and salads — offering something for everyone.
If you’re in Bandra, Freny’s is a must-visit spot for its heartwarming ambiance, nostalgic charm, and standout food & drinks. Can’t wait to go

featured_reviews.review_text:
Its simply just convenient. Nothing memorable

Cos of the veg array

I keep coming back to this vegetarian restaurant, and if I’m being honest, geography is doing a lot of the heavy lifting here. It’s conveniently close enough that my laziness can overpower my cravings for a while.

The food is fresh, well-made, and clearly prepared with care. The menu does a commendable job of convincing vegetables to impersonate things they were never meant to be. Some dishes even come dangerously close to making me forget about real food- meat.

Unfortunately, I was raised on a steady diet of creatures that once had opinions, so my deeply ingrained bias toward real food remains the ultimate buzzkill. Every bite is accompanied by a tiny voice in my head asking, “This is nice, but we paying
Fr veggie food bro?”

That said, if you’re vegetarian, you’ll probably love it. If you’re a carnivore like me, you’ll still enjoy it—especially if it’s close enough that convenience can temporarily defeat instinct.

Would return. Mostly because it’s nearby. Partly. Thats it
